seo_title: Mara River Camp | A tented camp in the Maasai Mara, Kenya | Exploreans
seo_description: A tented camp on a quiet bend of the Mara River, at the foot of the Oloololo Escarpment. Walk with Maasai guides at first light, follow the Great Migration from July to October and sleep beside the river.

hero.title: A tented camp on a quiet bend of the Mara River
hero.alt: The Mara River from above, elephants beside a safari vehicle, a table laid on the plains and a giraffe at the edge of the trees

story.label: What you will live
story.headline: The day begins on foot, with the river still in mist
story.text: Mara River Camp sits on {0}, at the foot of {1}. {2} pass through the camp itself, and from July to October {3} gathers at crossing points close by. {4} read the grass, the tracks and the birds, and share them at walking pace. Evenings end by the open fire, as the stars come out over the river.

day.label: A day at the camp
day.headline: From first light to the fire
day.lead: Every experience here is led by someone who knows the place by heart. This is how a day can unfold.

moments.body: The camp is still quiet. On the River Deck, gentle stretching and a few long breaths as the first light comes up over the water.
moments.alt: The wide brown water of the Mara River between wooded banks, below the camp

moments.body: From 6am the vehicle heads into the reserve, coffee in the flask. The engine goes quiet at the edge of the plains and elephants cross ahead.
moments.alt: Elephants grazing beside a safari vehicle on the open plains

moments.body: Near Olkiombo Airstrip, the camp kitchen cooks in the open: eggs to order, pastries, fruit and fresh coffee, with the plains all around.
moments.alt: The camp team laying a table with a red cloth on the plains beside the safari vehicles

moments.body: The heat settles and the camp goes quiet. A book, a swim and the sound of the river.
moments.alt: The camp swimming pool surrounded by sunbeds and trees, seen from above

moments.body: At 4.30pm the table is waiting at the Elephant’s Couch. Wine, cold Kenyan beer and warm bites as the sun drops behind the plains.
moments.alt: Sparkling wine poured into a glass against the low sun

moments.body: Back at camp, the pod shifts in the river below the River Deck as the light goes.
moments.alt: A pod of hippos resting in the brown water of the Mara River, seen from above

moments.body: The fire is lit on the River Deck. Stories from the Maasai team, and the hippos calling below in the dark.

people.label: The people
people.headline: Walking with the people who know it best
people.lead: The welcome begins at the gate, with Maasai hosts singing guests in from the vehicles. From then on, every walk, drive and table is led by someone from the camp.
people.alt: Maasai hosts in red shukas singing and jumping to welcome guests at the camp entrance

roles.body: They welcome guests to the camp in song and tell the stories around the fire. They read the grass, the tracks and the birds the way most of us read a page.
They lead the game drives, by day in the reserve and by spotlight in the Ole Sugut Conservancy, and know where the herds are likely to be before the vehicle leaves camp.
They cook breakfast in the open near Olkiombo, lay the sundowner at the Elephant’s Couch and keep the Zebra Bar open until bedtime.

stay.label: Rooms and spaces
stay.headline: Canvas, timber and the sound of the river
stay.lead: River tents along the bank, bush tents with room to spread out and a two-bedroom log cabin with a deck over the water.

closer.label: The place, specifically
closer.headline: Look closer at the river
closer.lead: From the air, the Mara River below camp is a ribbon of brown water. Look again and there is a pod of hippos, resting in the shallows.
closer.alt: A pod of hippos resting in the brown water of the Mara River, seen from above

passport.label: The Exploreans Passport
passport.headline: Your page at Mara River Camp
passport.lead: Every guest will receive an Exploreans Passport, stamped by the person who leads each experience. Collect one stamp in each of the five families and your Mara page is complete. Mark the experiences you would like and we will plan your days around them.
